7.1.5 It is heartening to note that we have been able to bring down female infant mortality rate considerably from 111 to 1981 to only 80 in 1991 which is almost of the same order as that male infant mortality rate. On the other hand, though the literacy amongst female children has improved over years it still falls short significantly in rate as compared to male children. However, the more disturbing phenomenon is the gradual decline in the proportion of female population in our country.
Legal Rights

7.2.1 To uphold the Constitutional mandate, the State has enacted various legislative measures intended to ensure equal rights, to counter social discrimination and various forms of violence and atrocities and to provide support services especially to working women.

7.2.2 Although Women may be victims in any of the crimes be it ‘Murder’, ‘Robbery’, ‘Cheating’ or any other crimes, the crimes which are directed specifically against Women are characterised as ‘Crime Against Women’. These are broadly classified under two categories.
(1) The Crimes Identified Under the Indian Penal Code (IPC)
(i) Rape (Sec. 376 IPC)
(ii) Kidnapping & Abduction for different purposes (Sec. 363 - 373 IPC)
(iii) Homicide for Dowry, Dowry Deaths or their attempts (Sec. 302/304-B IPC)
(iv) Torture, both mental and physical (Sec. 498-A IPC)
(v) Molestation (Sec. 354 IPC)
(vi) Sexual Harassment\(^{{*}}\) (Sec. 509 IPC)
(vii) Importation of girls (upto 21 years of age) (Sec. 366-B IPC)
(* referred in the past as ‘Eve-Teasing’)
(2) The Crimes identified under the Special Laws (SLL)

7.2.3 Although all laws are not gender specific, the provisions of law affecting women significantly have been reviewed periodically and amendments carried out to keep pace with emerging demands. The special social enactments to safeguard women and their interests, specifically are:
Custodial Rapes
7.4.6 . During the year 1996 only 6 cases of custodial rape i.e. 3 from Andhra Pradesh, 2 from Maharashtra and'l from Delhi were reported in the country.
Kidnapping & Abduction

7.4.7 Incidence of these cases reported an increase of 5.8 per cent in 1996 over 1995. The States of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan each reported nearly 17 per cent of these cases at national level while Delhi UT with share of 6.2% cases reported highest rate at 8.1.
Dowry Deaths

7.4.8 Incidence of Dowry Death cases reported an increase of 8.3 per cent over previous year. 36 per cent of these cases at national level were reported by Uttar Pradesh alone followed by Madhya Pradesh 10.5 per cent.
Torture (Cruelty by Husband & Relatives)

7.4.9 Incidence of Torture cases in the country increased by 13.2 per cent in 1996 over previous year. 26 per cent of these reported by Madhya Pradesh state with the highest rate in the country at 10.5.
Molestation

7.4.10 Incidence of Molestation cases in the country reported a marginal increase of 1.6 per cent over previous year. Nearly 24 per cent of total such cases were reported from Madhya Pradesh state. A significantly higher rate (9.8) than National Average rate (3.1) was reported from Sikkim state mainly because of its low population.
